title: Congress Questions Mohan Bhagwat’s Manipur Visit, Demands Action for Lasting Peace
summary: Manipur Congress CLP leader Keisham Meghachandra Singh questioned the purpose of RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's visit and called for a concrete roadmap for peace, rehabilitation and reconciliation.
body:
IMPHAL, November 19: Manipur Congress Legislature Party (CLP) leader Keisham Meghachandra Singh has questioned whether the three-day visit of Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat to Manipur will lead to concrete steps towards restoring peace in the violence-affected state.

In a statement shared on November 19, Singh said Manipur needed practical action rather than another round of assurances, particularly as thousands of families continue to face displacement, loss of livelihoods and uncertainty following the ethnic violence that began in May 2023.

Bhagwat arrived in Imphal on November 18 for a three-day visit scheduled to continue until November 20. According to an RSS functionary, his programme includes reviewing the organisation's activities and social initiatives in the state, as well as assessing programmes conducted as part of its centenary celebrations.

**Congress Leader Seeks Clarity on Purpose of Visit**

Reacting to Bhagwat's visit, Singh questioned whether the RSS chief would directly engage with displaced families and communities affected by the prolonged violence.

"Manipur needs peace, not just organisational meetings," Singh said, raising questions about whether the visit would contribute to restoring lasting peace and rebuilding trust among the Meitei, Kuki-Zo and Naga communities.

He also sought clarity on whether the RSS leadership would present a concrete roadmap for reconciliation and whether the visit would result in measurable outcomes to address the continuing crisis.

The Congress leader argued that organisational reviews and centenary programmes should not overshadow the suffering of people affected by the violence.

**Demands Rehabilitation and Accountability**

Singh highlighted the continuing humanitarian consequences of the conflict, including loss of lives, displacement of families, destruction of homes and damage to livelihoods.

He said thousands of people remained displaced, while many families continued to live with uncertainty and fear. Against this backdrop, he called for lasting peace, security, rehabilitation, accountability and a credible political roadmap.

The Congress CLP leader also questioned whether the RSS leadership would address the responsibility of the BJP-led political establishment for the prolonged crisis.

He argued that if the RSS leadership had influence over the BJP establishment, people had the right to expect that influence to be used to encourage meaningful steps towards peace, reconciliation and restoration of normalcy.

**Bhagwat's Visit Amid Continuing Crisis**

Bhagwat's visit comes as Manipur continues to deal with the consequences of the ethnic violence that erupted between Meitei and Kuki communities in May 2023.

According to figures cited in the India Today NE report, the violence has claimed at least 306 lives, while 49 people remain missing and thousands have been displaced.

The report also referred to separate clashes between Kuki and Naga groups in the hill districts since February 2026, which have reportedly claimed at least 50 lives.

The Congress leader's remarks have brought renewed attention to questions surrounding the role of influential national organisations in facilitating dialogue and reconciliation in Manipur.

While Bhagwat's announced programme is primarily organisational, Singh has called for the visit to be accompanied by meaningful engagement with affected communities and a clear approach towards addressing the state's continuing humanitarian and political challenges.

The outcome of the visit and whether it leads to any further engagement on peace and reconciliation remain to be seen.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
